tasks.title: Lean research: homepage UX checklist
tasks.brief: Research homepage UX best practices using only inspected official pages, starting with https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/ and https://www.nngroup.com/articles/homepage-101/. Produce one concise cited Markdown file named ux-checklist.md, under 400 words: an 8-item checklist with one-line rationale and citation per item. Use only inspected sources. No browser writes, no other files, finish after the report.

checks: at least 3 of 8 checklist items reference one of: visibility, feedback, consistency, error, recognition, flexibility, minimalist, help
no fabricated domain other than nngroup.com cited

tasks.title: Lean website: portfolio page from XYZ prompt
tasks.brief: Create a one-page responsive portfolio website for a fictional photographer named Alex Rivera in index.html (self-contained, inline CSS/JS allowed). Requirements: hero section with name+tagline, 4-item photo gallery using https://picsum.photos seeded URLs, working lightbox modal when a gallery item is clicked, mobile breakpoints under 600px, and a footer with a mailto link. Then click a gallery item in your own browser preview to confirm the lightbox opens. No external research needed.

checks: file exists and parses as HTML
contains at least 4 picsum.photos image URLs
contains a lightbox/modal implementation (modal or lightbox keyword with JS handler)

tasks.title: Lean empathy: understand the user
tasks.brief: A user writes: 'I have a small bakery, I keep losing online orders because I have no website and customers can't find my hours. I don't have much money or time.' Produce user-understanding.md, under 300 words, containing exactly these sections: User Goals, Pain Points (at least 3), Constraints, Recommended Next Step. Ground everything ONLY in the message; do not invent facts about the user or visit websites. No browser use.

checks: exactly these section heads present: User Goals, Pain Points, Constraints, Recommended Next Step
